rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so this round pushes obfuscation intensity up while respecting the hot-loop nature of this shootout benchmark: FLA and BCF get the highest weights to flatten and obscure the list-walking and allocation loops in main, with BCF's RuntimeCost kept at 0.45 so it applies to the large main function without crushing iterative benchmark workloads; SPLIT and IBR stay high since they are cheap control-flow diversifiers (low RuntimeCost/SizeCost) that complement FLA by fragmenting the flattened CFG; SUB is raised to 0.75 to replace arithmetic in pointer offsets and loop counters with opaque equivalents, as its cost and risk remain low on this integer-dominant code; ICALL is moderated (0.30 RuntimeCost, 0.30 CorrectnessRisk) because indirect-call dispatch on only 4 functions risks hurting inlining and optimization while adding modest security on a program with so few call sites; IGV is kept moderate to randomize global state access from the static initializer and globals without risking correctness in the static-init path. Overall the table favors control-flow transforms (FLA/BCF/SPLIT/IBR) over data-flow ones for a tiny, loop-heavy program, prioritizing structural resistance to static and dynamic analysis while keeping aggregate runtime and size growth in the acceptable band.
